target.title: feat(discord): support multiple file attachments per message (fixes #24196)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #24196.

Discord API allows up to 10 file attachments per message, but the integration only supported a single `mediaUrl`.

## Changes Made

1. **send.outbound.ts**: Added `mediaUrls?: string[]` to `DiscordSendOpts`. Auto-batches >10 files across multiple messages. Reply reference only on first batch.
2. **sendDiscordMedia** (`send.shared.ts`): Accepts `mediaUrls: string[]` — iterates all URLs into a single `files` array for Discord's multipart upload.
3. **outbound-payload.ts**: Multiple media URLs batch into one `sendMessageDiscord` call. Component messages reject multiple attachments with a clear error.
4. **send.components.ts**: Added `mediaUrls` to component opts. Classic mode forwards to batch send.
5. **Tests**: 57/57 pass. Coverage for 3-file batch, >10 auto-split with replyTo behavior, legacy backward compatibility.

## Evidence

### Real Discord API — 12 files auto-split into 2 messages
```
Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
Time: 2026-07-03T12:34:26Z

--- 12 JPEG files via mediaUrls[] ---
Final messageId: 1522581296595996764
Receipt kind: media

=== PASS: 12 files auto-split into 2 messages ===
```

Batch 1: 10 files with caption. Batch 2: 2 files, no text, no reply reference.

### Unit tests (57/57 passed)
| Scenario | Result |
|---------|--------|
| 3 files via mediaUrls[] in one message | ✅ |
| 12 files auto-split into 2 messages | ✅ |
| ReplyTo only on first batch | ✅ |
| Legacy single mediaUrl | ✅ |
| Components + >1 mediaUrl → error | ✅ |

## AI Assistance
- AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: feat(google): restore Antigravity and harden Gemini auth boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This PR restores first-class Google auth replacement support for the three Google provider paths that currently matter:

- `google-antigravity` uses the signed-in Antigravity/`agy` session and runs prompts through `agy --print`.
- `google-gemini-cli` imports the official Gemini CLI OAuth cache and validates the active account identity before using it.
- `google` remains the Gemini API-key provider.

The important boundary is that Google credentials stay provider-owned. OpenClaw does not start its own Google browser callback for Antigravity, and it does not import or persist raw Google OAuth tokens from Antigravity. For Antigravity, OAuth/session ownership stays with the Antigravity/`agy` session.

This also hardens the shared Google auth replacement boundary. Gemini CLI OAuth cache import now requires validated active Google account identity before credential material is saved, refreshed, forwarded, or staged. Legacy `google-gemini-cli` OAuth profiles missing account identity are recovered through the official Gemini CLI cache when the imported account matches the expected profile identity; otherwise they fail closed.

## What Changed

Antigravity:

- Added bundled `google-antigravity` provider registration.
- Added a `google-antigravity` CLI backend.
- Routed `google-antigravity` prompts through `agy --print` with a bounded print timeout.
- Added Antigravity setup that creates a local `google-antigravity:antigravity-session` auth profile from the signed-in Antigravity app/session boundary.
- Added runtime auth resolution for the Antigravity app-session profile.
- Added external/synthetic auth handling so OpenClaw can identify the Antigravity session without importing raw Google OAuth tokens.
- Added Antigravity provider aliases and Google provider model/policy wiring.
- Updated setup notes to make the boundary explicit: Antigravity owns the Google OAuth session; OpenClaw delegates execution to `agy`.

Gemini CLI:

- Added official Gemini CLI cache import support for `google-gemini-cli`.
- Changed `google-gemini-cli` setup to import the official Gemini CLI cache instead of launching an OpenClaw-owned Google browser auth flow.
- Required validated active Gemini CLI Google account identity during cache import.
- Added compatibility handling for legacy `google-gemini-cli` OAuth profiles that lack identity by recovering identity from the official Gemini CLI cache when it matches the expected profile.
- Failed closed when Gemini CLI account identity is missing or mismatched.
- Failed closed before save, refresh, forwarding, or runtime staging when account identity does not match.
- Preserved isolated Gemini CLI auth-home staging.
- Preserved inherited Google auth env clearing.

Shared auth/backend boundary:

- Added provider-owned CLI backend auth resolution through `resolveCliBackendAuthCredential`.
- Preserved generic fallback forwarding only when no provider-owned hook exists.
- Made provider hook decline fail closed instead of falling through to generic forwarding.
- Preserved backend allowlist checks before and after auth resolution.
- Preserved Gemini API-key staging for `google` API-key profiles.
- Fixed CLI runner cleanup gaps on mid-prepare failures.
- Updated Google provider docs, live-testing docs, Plugin SDK exports/API baseline, and CLI backend plugin docs.

## Evidence

Antigravity headless behavior:

```text
agy -h
agy models
agy --print 'Reply exactly: OPENCLAW_AGY_PRINT_OK' --print-timeout 2m0s
```

Result: `agy --print` returned `OPENCLAW_AGY_PRINT_OK`.

Sterile-home Antigravity session behavior:

```text
HOME="$PROOF_HOME" ANTIGRAVITY_USER_DATA_DIR="$HOME/.config/Antigravity" agy --print 'Reply exactly: OPENCLAW_AGY_STERILE_OK' --print-timeout 2m0s
```

Result: `agy --print` returned `OPENCLAW_AGY_STERILE_OK` while running under the isolated proof `HOME`. This verifies that the runtime can use the Antigravity session boundary through `ANTIGRAVITY_USER_DATA_DIR` instead of relying on the operator's normal home directory.

OpenClaw Antigravity runtime behavior:

```text
HOME="$PROOF_HOME" \
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH="$PROOF_CONFIG" \
ANTIGRAVITY_USER_DATA_DIR="$HOME/.config/Antigravity" \
pnpm openclaw qa manual \
  --provider-mode live-frontier \
  --model google-antigravity/gemini-3-flash \
  --message 'Reply exactly: OPENCLAW_AGY_OPENCLAW_OK' \
  --timeout-ms 240000
```

Result: OpenClaw returned status `ok` with reply `OPENCLAW_AGY_OPENCLAW_OK`.

Focused validation:

```text
pnpm test extensions/google/index-harness-registration.test.ts extensions/google/setup-api.test.ts extensions/google/index.test.ts src/agents/cli-backends.test.ts src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts
```

Result: passed. Agents shard: 87 tests passed. Extension-providers shard: 32 tests passed. Total focused tests: 119 passed.

```text
pnpm check:test-types
```

Result: passed.

```text
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check
```

Result: passed. `OK docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256`.

```text
pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check
```

Result: passed. Public SDK surface check passed with no package-exported forbidden subpaths.

```text
git diff --check
```

Result: passed.

Gemini CLI behavior:

- Official Gemini CLI cache import through OpenClaw succeeds and creates a `google-gemini-cli/<account>` OAuth profile from the official cache.
- OpenClaw runtime reaches the `google-gemini-cli` OAuth path when invoked with a `google-gemini-cli/...` model ref.
- The live Gemini CLI account used for proof is blocked upstream by Google's `IneligibleTierError`/unsupported-client gate. A direct official `gemini` CLI control run hits the same upstream eligibility gate, which confirms the remaining failure is upstream account/client eligibility rather than OpenClaw auth routing.

## Owner Acceptance

Provider owner acceptance: pending.

Plugin SDK owner acceptance: pending.

Security owner acceptance: pending.

Maintainer acceptance for the Google auth replacement boundary and provider-owned credential handling: pending.

## What Was Not Tested

I did not run the full repository test suite. The focused suites cover the changed Google provider registration, Antigravity setup/runtime behavior, Gemini CLI account identity validation, CLI auth forwarding boundary, types, SDK surface, and proof behavior.

I did not prove successful Gemini CLI model generation with the live account. The changed OpenClaw path reaches Gemini CLI OAuth runtime, but the installed official Gemini CLI and account are blocked by Google's upstream unsupported-client/eligibility gate.

I did not prove model-specific Antigravity selection through `agy --model`. The current Antigravity proof shows that OpenClaw routes `google-antigravity/gemini-3-flash` through the `agy --print` runtime and receives a response. A follow-up can map OpenClaw model refs to exact `agy models` display names and pass `--model` explicitly.

The targeted gateway live harness still has a known limitation for explicit provider-scoped sweeps: that path suppresses external/synthetic auth profiles during auth preflight before CLI backend execution. The product/runtime proof is therefore captured with `pnpm openclaw qa manual`, which reaches the actual `google-antigravity` backend and returns the expected response.

## Tests

AI-assisted: yes.

## Real behavior proof

Latest Antigravity proof files:

- `/home/rev/pr-98343-antigravity-current-proof/15-agy-headless-print-proof.txt`
- `/home/rev/pr-98343-antigravity-current-proof/16-agy-sterile-home-proof.txt`
- `/home/rev/pr-98343-antigravity-current-proof/17-openclaw-agy-runtime-proof.txt`

Real Antigravity behavior proven:

- `agy -h` exposes non-interactive `--print` mode and `--print-timeout`.
- `agy models` lists the Antigravity model surface.
- Direct `agy --print 'Reply exactly: OPENCLAW_AGY_PRINT_OK'` returns `OPENCLAW_AGY_PRINT_OK`.
- `agy --print` works under a sterile proof `HOME` when `ANTIGRAVITY_USER_DATA_DIR` points at the signed-in Antigravity session.
- OpenClaw `qa manual --model google-antigravity/gemini-3-flash` routes through the `google-antigravity` backend and returns `OPENCLAW_AGY_OPENCLAW_OK`.
- OpenClaw does not import or persist raw Google OAuth tokens for Antigravity. OAuth/session ownership stays with the Antigravity/`agy` session.

Real Gemini CLI behavior proven:

- OpenClaw imports the official Gemini CLI OAuth cache through the `google-gemini-cli` setup path.
- OpenClaw validates the imported account identity before saving or using the profile.
- Legacy identity-missing `google-gemini-cli` profiles can recover through the official cache when the imported identity matches the expected profile.
- Mismatched or missing identity fails closed.
- OpenClaw reaches the changed `google-gemini-cli` OAuth runtime path; the live account is then blocked by Google's upstream unsupported-client/eligibility gate, matching the direct official Gemini CLI control failure.

target.title: fix: add resilient fallback policy for user model overrides
target.body:
## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2–5 bullets:

- Problem: session/user model overrides always disabled configured fallback chains.
- Why it matters: operators could configure provider fallback behavior, but a user-selected model had no fallback safety net during transient provider/model failures.
- What changed: adds opt-in `userOverrideFallbackPolicy: "resilient"` on `agents.defaults.model` and per-agent chat model config, with schema/types/help/labels/docs and fallback-resolution tests.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): default behavior remains `strict`; auto-selected model overrides and configured agent primaries keep their existing fallback behavior; non-chat model config schemas remain unchanged.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes N/A
- Related N/A
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: a user/session model override can now inherit the configured fallback chain when the new policy is explicitly set to `resilient`, while the default `strict` behavior still returns no fallbacks.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw checkout on pop-os, Node v25.8.1, branch `fix/user-override-fallback-policy`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  ```bash
  pnpm exec tsx -e 'import { resolveEffectiveModelFallbacks } from "./src/agents/agent-scope.ts"; const cfg={agents:{defaults:{model:{primary:"openai/gpt-5.4",fallbacks:["anthropic/claude-haiku-3-5","google/gemini-2.5-flash"],userOverrideFallbackPolicy:"resilient"}},list:[{id:"linus"}]}}; console.log("user override resilient =>", JSON.stringify(resolveEffectiveModelFallbacks({cfg,agentId:"linus",hasSessionModelOverride:true,modelOverrideSource:"user"}))); const strict={agents:{defaults:{model:{primary:"openai/gpt-5.4",fallbacks:["anthropic/claude-haiku-3-5"]}},list:[{id:"linus"}]}}; console.log("user override strict =>", JSON.stringify(resolveEffectiveModelFallbacks({cfg:strict,agentId:"linus",hasSessionModelOverride:true,modelOverrideSource:"user"})));'
  ```
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):
  ```text
  user override resilient => ["anthropic/claude-haiku-3-5","google/gemini-2.5-flash"]
  user override strict => []
  ```
- Observed result after fix: resilient user overrides receive the configured fallback list; strict user overrides receive an empty fallback list.
- What was not tested: live provider failover against real external model APIs, because that would require changing a running gateway config. The changed resolver and config schema were tested locally.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): covered by the existing and new regression tests: the pre-change resolver returned `[]` for user overrides whenever `hasSessionModelOverride` was true.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

For bug fixes or regressions, explain why this happened, not just what changed. Otherwise write `N/A`. If the cause is unclear, write `Unknown`.

- Root cause: `resolveEffectiveModelFallbacks` treated every non-auto session model override as authoritative and returned an empty fallback list without a config escape hatch.
- Missing detection / guardrail: no regression coverage for user-selected models that should intentionally keep operator-configured fallback chains.
- Contributing context (if known): auto model overrides and user/session overrides were represented in the same resolver path, but operators need separate fallback policy for user choices.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

For bug fixes or regressions, name the smallest reliable test coverage that should catch this. Otherwise write `N/A`.

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts`, `src/config/zod-schema.agent-defaults.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: user model overrides remain strict by default, can opt into resilient fallback inheritance, and per-agent policy overrides defaults.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the behavior is selected in the config schema and resolved in the agent-scope fallback helper before provider execution.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): N/A
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users can set `userOverrideFallbackPolicy: "resilient"` under `agents.defaults.model` or an individual agent's chat `model` block. The default is still `strict`.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[user override] -> [fallbacks disabled]

After:
[user override] -> [strict policy] -> [fallbacks disabled]
[user override] -> [resilient policy] -> [configured fallbacks preserved]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: pop-os Linux
- Runtime/container: local Node v25.8.1 / pnpm
- Model/provider: N/A, pure config + fallback resolver change
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted): `agents.defaults.model.userOverrideFallbackPolicy: "resilient"`

### Steps

1. Configure fallback models under `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`.
2. Set `agents.defaults.model.userOverrideFallbackPolicy: "resilient"`.
3. Resolve fallbacks for a session/user model override.

### Expected

- Resilient user overrides inherit configured fallback models.
- Strict/default user overrides keep fallback models disabled.

### Actual

- Matches expected in the local resolver smoke and targeted tests.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Verification commands run:

```text
codex review --base origin/main
pnpm check:changed
pnpm test src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts src/config/zod-schema.agent-defaults.test.ts
pnpm config:docs:check && pnpm config:schema:check
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
```

`codex review --base origin/main` result:

```text
The change consistently adds the new user override fallback policy across config types, schema validation, labels/help, docs, and fallback resolution. I did not find a discrete correctness issue in the modified paths.
```

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios: strict default, resilient defaults, per-agent policy override, explicit fallback override behavior, config schema acceptance/rejection, generated config docs/schema consistency.
- Edge cases checked: explicit empty fallback list still disables fallback inheritance; non-chat model schemas still reject the chat-only policy field.
- What you did **not** verify: live external provider outage failover through a running gateway.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`) Yes, optional new config field
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: set `userOverrideFallbackPolicy: "resilient"` only when user-selected models should keep configured fallback chains.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: operators may expect resilient behavior after adding fallbacks but forget the new policy.
  - Mitigation: docs and schema help call out the strict default and the explicit opt-in field.
